note: deltaB = first-year change to the deficit, $B; positive reduces the deficit. Mostly 10-year scores divided by 10 (CBO 'Options for Reducing the Deficit', Dec 2024, unless noted). Approximate. households = rough annual $ change for each archetype (+ = better off).

policies.label: 5% broad-based VAT
policies.source: CBO Options (annualized)

policies.label: $25/ton carbon tax (no rebate)
policies.source: CBO Options (annualized)

policies.label: Carbon dividend: $40/ton carbon tax, all rebated per person
policies.source: Revenue-neutral by design. Most low- and middle-income households get back more than they pay.

policies.label: Restore EV tax credits ($7,500/car)
policies.source: Ended Sept 2025 by P.L. 119-21. Usage ran well above CBO's original score.

policies.label: Restore all clean-energy tax credits repealed in 2025
policies.source: Low confidence: estimates vary ~3x (CBO 2022 vs Penn Wharton/Goldman). Includes EV credits.

policies.label: Repeal the remaining clean-energy credits (nuclear, carbon capture, clean fuels, manufacturing)
policies.source: Low confidence; what's left after P.L. 119-21's cuts.

policies.label: Repeal fossil-fuel tax breaks
policies.source: Intangible drilling costs, percentage depletion, etc.

policies.label: Nuclear buildout (federal financing for new reactors)
policies.source: Low confidence; depends on the federal share. Vogtle units 3-4 cost ~$35B.

policies.label: Green New Deal-style clean energy & grid investment
policies.source: Uses Biden's 2020 climate plan ($2T over 4 years) as the scorable core. The GND resolution itself has no official score.

policies.label: 2% wealth tax above $50M
policies.source: Advocates' estimate; heavily contested (valuation, avoidance)

policies.label: Tax unrealized gains at death
policies.source: Treasury Green Book (annualized)

policies.label: Tax carried interest as ordinary income
policies.source: CBO/JCT (annualized)

policies.label: +$10B/yr IRS enforcement
policies.source: CBO (net of cost; ramps up over time)

policies.label: Raise fuel taxes 15¢/gal
policies.source: CBO Options (annualized)

policies.label: Eliminate the federal diesel tax (24.4¢/gal)
policies.source: Tax Policy Center: diesel excise raised ~$10.8B (FY2023). An Oct 2026 executive order defers it through Dec 31; this makes it permanent.

policies.label: Repeal the remaining 2025 tariffs
policies.source: MTS FY2026: net customs $173B vs ~$80B before 2025 (gross $318B less $145B refunded after the IEEPA tariffs were struck down)

policies.label: Raise the stock-buyback tax from 1% to 4%
policies.source: Treasury Green Book (~$166B over 10 years).

policies.label: 0.1% tax on stock, bond & derivative trades
policies.source: CBO Options: ~$777B over 2019-28 (JCT). Disputed: trading volume would fall, so actual revenue could be much lower.

policies.label: Sell $1M 'Gold Card' residency visas
policies.source: Low confidence. ~10,000 registered interest at launch (Dec 2025); 10,000/yr x $1M = $10B. Official claims bundle it into $100B with other programs.

policies.label: Stop the Fed paying interest on bank reserves
policies.source: Low confidence. Cruz claims $1.1T over 10 yrs; critics say banks would shift into T-bills and savings would be small. Midpoint-ish.

policies.label: Sell government stakes in Fannie Mae & Freddie Mac
policies.source: Low confidence. Reported plans to sell ~5% for ~$30B.

policies.label: Repeal remaining CHIPS Act subsidies (unspent grants + 35% chip-factory credit)
policies.source: Low confidence. CHIPS (2022) gave $39B in factory grants, mostly awarded, and a 25% investment credit CBO scored at ~$24B/10yr; OBBBA raised it to 35% for projects started by end-2026, with no published JCT score.

policies.label: Repeal no-tax-on-tips & overtime deductions
policies.source: JCT score of P.L. 119-21 (annualized)

policies.label: Restore $10k SALT cap (from $40k)
policies.source: JCT score of P.L. 119-21 (annualized)

policies.label: Billionaire minimum tax (25% incl. unrealized gains, $100M+)
policies.source: Treasury FY2025 Green Book: ~$500B over 10 years.

policies.label: Use chained CPI for SS cost-of-living raises
policies.source: CBO Options (annualized; grows each year)

policies.label: Raise full retirement age to 70 (phased in)
policies.source: CBO Options (small at first; large long-run savings)

policies.label: No income tax on Social Security benefits
policies.source: CRFB: ~$1.8T over FY2026-35, all of it revenue that now goes to the Social Security and Medicare trust funds, so it speeds up their insolvency.

policies.label: Means-test benefits for high-income retirees
policies.source: Low confidence. Phases down benefits for retirees with high non-Social Security income.

policies.label: Cut Medicare Advantage benchmarks
policies.source: CBO Options (annualized)

policies.label: Expand Medicare drug price negotiation
policies.source: CBO (annualized, approx.)

policies.label: Per-capita caps on federal Medicaid funding
policies.source: CBO Options (annualized)

policies.label: Restore enhanced ACA subsidies
policies.source: CBO (annualized)

policies.label: Site-neutral Medicare payments + pharmacy-benefit-manager reform
policies.source: CBO: site-neutral options ~$140B over 10 yrs; PBM reforms ~$5B/yr.

policies.label: Cut farm subsidies & crop insurance
policies.source: CBO Options (annualized)

policies.label: Freeze federal civilian pay for one year
policies.source: CBO (approx.)

policies.label: Close most overseas military bases
policies.source: Low confidence. Overseas basing is ~$55B/yr (2021 est.), but host-nation support and relocating forces home cut the net savings.

policies.label: End foreign aid (economic & humanitarian)
policies.source: ~1% of the budget. Polls find Americans guess it's ~25%.

policies.label: Resume Ukraine aid at the 2022–24 pace
policies.source: Low confidence. Congress appropriated ~$175B for Ukraine over 2022–24 (about half military); little new aid is in the FY2026 baseline. Outlays lag appropriations.

policies.label: End military aid to Israel
policies.source: 2016 U.S.–Israel MOU: $3.3B/yr in Foreign Military Financing plus $0.5B for missile defense (FY2019–28). Excludes one-time wartime supplementals.

policies.label: Abolish the Department of Education (programs move elsewhere)
policies.source: Low confidence. Proposals move Pell grants, Title I and special-ed funding to other agencies, so savings are mostly overhead.

policies.label: Mass deportation program
policies.source: American Immigration Council: ~$88B/yr in enforcement costs. Lost tax revenue from deported workers is not counted.

policies.label: Immigration reform with a path to legal status
policies.source: CBO (S.744, 2013): cut deficits ~$175B in the first decade as more workers pay taxes.

policies.label: Renew the 2021 infrastructure law's funding
policies.source: IIJA added ~$550B of new spending over FY2022-26 (~$110B/yr). Actual outlays lag spending authority.

policies.label: Expand CTC to 2021 levels, fully refundable
policies.source: CBO/JCT (annualized)

policies.label: Universal pre-K
policies.source: Approx. (2021 Build Back Better proposal, annualized)

policies.label: Tuition-free public college
policies.source: Sanders' College for All Act (2021): ~$47B/yr federal share.

policies.label: Universal childcare (cost capped ~7% of income)
policies.source: CBO score of the 2021 House bill: ~$380B over 10 years.

policies.label: 12 weeks of national paid family leave
policies.source: White House estimate: ~$225B over 10 years.

policies.label: Baby bonds ($1,000 at birth + up to $2,000/yr by income)
policies.source: CRFB: ~$650B over 10 years. Paid into accounts, not cash, until age 18.

policies.label: Extend Trump Accounts' $1,000 baby deposit past 2028
policies.source: ~3.6M births x $1,000, plus the tax break on contributions (not counted). Taxes on withdrawals decades later pay back part, beyond this model's horizon.

policies.label: Housing supply package (expand housing tax credit & builder incentives)
policies.source: Low confidence. Combines proposals to expand the Low-Income Housing Tax Credit and new-construction incentives.

policies.label: Defense budget to $1.5 trillion
policies.source: FY2027 request: ~$1.15T base + $350B via reconciliation. Scored as outlays rising from FY2026's $965B; real outlays would ramp up over several years.

policies.label: Medicare for All
policies.source: Urban Institute (2019): ~$34T more federal spending over 10 years. Unfunded here; households would also stop paying premiums (not shown).

policies.label: Forgive $10k–$20k of student debt
policies.source: CBO (2022): ~$400B one-time cost. Struck down by the Supreme Court in 2023.

policies.label: $25k down-payment aid for first-time buyers
policies.source: Campaign estimate ~$100B over four years.

policies.label: Buffett Rule: 30% minimum tax on $1M+ incomes
policies.source: JCT (2012): ~$47B over 10 years, scaled up for income growth.

policies.label: 50¢/gal gas tax increase
policies.source: Scaled from CBO's 15¢ option (~$22B/yr), allowing for lower demand.

policies.label: 'Penny Plan': cut all non-interest spending 1%
policies.source: 1% of FY2026 non-interest outlays (~$6.3T). The plan repeats the cut every year.

policies.label: Abolish the income tax, replace it with tariffs
policies.source: Loses $2.85T of individual income tax. Clausing & Obstfeld (2024) put the revenue-maximizing tariff at ~$780B/yr. Household effects not shown.

policies.label: Roll back the One Big Beautiful Bill (2025)
policies.source: Restores pre-2025 law: TCJA brackets/deduction/CTC expire, no tips/overtime/senior deductions, Medicaid & SNAP cuts reversed. Total = CBO's FY2026 score (~$487B); the tax pieces are modeled directly, the rest is a lump sum.

policies.label: Roll back DOGE cuts
policies.source: Low confidence. Independent estimates of DOGE's verifiable net savings: ~$1-7B (B. Stevenson), ~$2B verified (NPR), ~$5.5B (OpenFeds); GAO-26-108615 could trace only 43% of claimed contract savings. Midpoint used. Excludes possible lost IRS revenue from staff cuts (estimates unverified).

policies.label: Federal jobs guarantee
policies.source: Low confidence. Outside estimates ~$400-500B/yr, depending on take-up and wages.

policies.label: $15 federal minimum wage
policies.source: CBO (2021): small budget effect; raises pay for ~17M workers, with ~1.4M fewer jobs.

policies.label: Start a sovereign wealth fund ($100B/yr, borrowed)
policies.source: Buying assets counts as spending, and the US borrows to do it. It pays off only if returns beat the Treasury rate (historically stocks beat it ~3-4 pts/yr, with risk). Most of that comes after this model's 10 years.
